questions.question: A data frame `df` was made with `data.frame()`, and afterwards the student runs `library(tidyverse)`. What is `df` then?
options: a tibble, since attaching the tidyverse converts all data frames
still a plain data frame, until `as_tibble(df)` converts it
still a data frame, but now printed with a type row like a tibble
a data frame for good, as only newly made tables can be tibbles

questions.question: A tibble has 40 columns, far more than fit across the console. What does printing it show?
options: all 40 columns, wrapped over several blocks of lines
only the first 10 columns, the same limit as for rows
only the columns that fit the width of the console
an error asking to select fewer columns before printing

questions.question: After `library(tidyverse)`, a student needs the time-series `filter()` of the stats package. Which call reaches it?
options: `stats::filter(...)`, with the package named in front
`filter(...)`, as base R packages always take priority
`library(stats)` followed by a plain `filter(...)`
`dplyr::filter(...)`, which hands time series to stats

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, `tb` is a tibble. Why do base R functions written for data frames, such as `nrow(tb)` and `str(tb)`, work on it without any conversion?
options: Attaching the tidyverse replaces them by versions written for tibbles.
A tibble is also a data frame: its class vector ends in `"data.frame"`.
Each such call permanently turns `tb` into a plain data frame.
A tibble stores its columns as one matrix, which these functions accept.

questions.question: A data frame `df` has a column `price` with values such as `12.3456`. After `tb <- as_tibble(df)`, which statement about `tb` is correct?
options: It holds the same values; only printing and behaviour differ.
It stores `price` rounded to the few digits a tibble prints.
It holds only the first 10 rows, the ones a tibble prints.
It turns `price` into a character column, as tibbles store text.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, how many data rows does the console show when printing `tibble(x = 1:15)`, and when printing `tibble(x = 1:25)`?
options: 10 and 10
15 and 20
15 and 25
15 and 10

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, which type labels does the printout of `tibble(a = 1:3, b = c(1, 2, 3), c = c("x", "y", "z"))` show under the columns `a`, `b` and `c`?
With the tidyverse attached and `df <- data.frame(x = 1:3)`, what does `class(as_tibble(df))` return?
options: `[1] "tibble"     "data.frame"`
`[1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"`
`[1] "data.frame"`
`[1] "tbl_df" "tbl"    "tibble"`

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, `tb <- tibble(x = 1:25, y = 0)` is printed. Its first line, above the column names, states the size of the table. Which size does it report?
options: 25 rows and 2 columns
10 rows and 2 columns
2 rows and 25 columns
15 rows and 2 columns

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `tb <- tibble(id = c(1, 2, 3), x = c(4, 8, 6))`, which call returns the values of `x` as a numeric vector?
In a fresh R session in which `library(tidyverse)` has not been run, a data frame `co2` with a column `Year` exists. `filter(co2, Year == 2021)` stops with `object 'Year' not found`. Why?
options: `filter()` needs a tibble, and `co2` is still a plain data frame.
Outside the tidyverse, column names must be written in quotes.
Plain `filter` here is the time-series filter of stats, not dplyr's.
R finds no function `filter` and reports the unknown `Year` instead.

questions.question: A data frame `df` has a column `code` holding the text values `"1"`, `"2"` and `"3"`, and `tb <- as_tibble(df)`. When both are printed, what shows that `code` is text?
options: Both printouts show the values in quotes, as `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`.
Only the tibble shows it, with `<chr>` in the row under the column name.
Only the data frame shows it, as it prints the text values in quotes.
Neither: both print `1 2 3`, and only `str()` reveals the type.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, `tb` is a tibble with 25 rows and 2 columns. What does `print(tb, n = 3)` show?
options: the first 3 rows and a closing line reporting 22 more rows
the first 3 rows and nothing after them
the first 10 rows, since `n` only matters for data frames
the first 3 columns, with all 25 rows

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `tb <- tibble(x = c(4, "n/a", 7))`, what does `sum(tb[["x"]])` return?
options: `[1] 11`, skipping the text entry
`[1] NA`, reading `"n/a"` as missing
an error, because `x` is a character column
`[1] "4n/a7"`, joining the entries as text

questions.question: A data frame `df` and a tibble `tb` both have a numeric column `Year` and no other column whose name starts with `Yea`. What does the dollar operator with the misspelt name `Yea` return for each?
options: `df`: the `Year` column; `tb`: `NULL` with a warning
`df`: `NULL` with a warning; `tb`: the `Year` column
both: the `Year` column, matched by its first letters
both: `NULL`, since no column is called `Yea`

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, which type label does the printout of `tibble(x = c(1, TRUE, NA))` show under `x`?
options: `<lgl>`
`<chr>`
`<dbl>`
`<int>`

questions.question: Code containing `median(d[, "price"])` returned the median price when `d` came from `read.csv()` on a file. After switching to `d <- read_csv()` on the same file, that line stops with the error `need numeric data`. Why?
options: `read_csv()` reads `price` as text, so the median of text is undefined.
`d[, "price"]` is now a one-column tibble, not a numeric vector.
`read_csv()` changes the column names, so `"price"` matches no column.
Tibbles refuse base R functions such as `median()` and `mean()`.

questions.question: A script runs `library(tidyverse)` and then `library(pkgB)`, where pkgB is an installed package that also has a function called `filter()`. Which `filter()` does a plain `filter(...)` call use afterwards?
options: dplyr's, as the tidyverse was attached first and keeps its names
stats' version, as base R functions take priority over packages
none: R stops and asks which of the versions is meant
pkgB's, as the package attached most recently wins

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, which type labels does the printout of `tibble(a = c(NA, NA), b = c(2L, NA), c = c(TRUE, NA))` show under `a`, `b` and `c`?
In a fresh session a student runs only `library(tibble)`, not `library(tidyverse)`. Which of these calls then stops with `could not find function`?
options: `tibble(x = 1:3)`
`as_tibble(data.frame(x = 1:3))`
`nrow(tibble(x = 1:3))`
`read_csv("sales.csv")`
